title: Instructions for the cipher with Baron Stosch and Mr Walton, TNA SP 106/7 (DECODE R597)

documents.route: Secretary of State's office -> a British correspondent (to write to Stosch/Walton)

plaintext.source: The writer wrote the syllable over every code group of the worked example and gave the plaintext sentence in clear.

transcription.notes: 43 = 30 groups Key A + 13 Key B, counted by hand; the run-on repetition not counted. Full text in transcription.txt.

system.summary: Syllabic code of three-digit groups 100-999 in two keys A and B used alternately, 371 signalling the change of key; groups run on without separation; 110, 220 &c. and all above 900 are nulls.
system.notes: Only the worked example's groups are known; keys A and B themselves not on the record.

prior_solution.where: DECODE record note describes the sheet (letter-pair nomenclator) but calls lines unsolved; the interlinear syllables are the writer's own.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, posed the target with /goal from the catalogue. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata for R597 and R598 and the two R597 images with the stored cookie.
Recognised the record as an English instruction sheet with a worked French example, not a ciphered letter; transcribed it, including the interlinear syllables over every group.
Identified DECODE's 'unsolved lines' as the same Key B example written run-on without separators.
Dated the sheet c. 1731 from Stosch (alias John Walton) and the correction Rome -> Florence.

outcome.method_basis: R597 is an English instruction sheet for the Stosch-Walton cipher with a worked French example whose syllables are written over every group; it is not a ciphered letter.
outcome.notes: Whole sheet read; 702 (du/up), 023 and the run-on digit doubtful.
